ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher and send the driver's account for review of the "I'm Here" tap made 600 m from the pickup + flag_account
ruling.reasoning: The driver cancelled at 12:09:25 and $6.61 was charged as a rider no-show [F3][F6], so NS-0 routes the case to NS-1/NS-2: the fee stands only if the arrival and waiting elements are met [NS-0]. The trace settles NS-1(i) as satisfied — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 [F5] — but NS-1(ii) fails: at that moment the GPS placed him 600 m from the pickup, and his closest approach over the whole trip was 599 m, never inside 200 m [F5][F1]. NS-1(iii) fails as well: he stayed within the 200 m radius for 0 s after the tap, so no continuous 3-minute wait at the pick-up location can be shown [F5]; his stationary 3 min 30 s was spent 600 m away [F2]. With (ii) and (iii) unmet, NS-2 gives the rider the full return of the $6.61 [NS-2], payable as a Ryde voucher and within the rider's dispute window [NS-7]. The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, and system records prevail over statements; the null driver_arrived_at corroborates that the platform never placed him at the pickup [F4]. Because he tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, NS-2 also requires the account flag [F5][F1][NS-2]. The rider's own chat message at 12:07 confirms she was at the pickup point and saw no car [F9], consistent with the GPS. Traffic on Jalan Besar at band 3 with no incidents and fair weather [F13][F14][F15] explains nothing about a stationary driver 600 m from the pickup and is not a "reasonable cause" screen for an NS-1 (ii)/(iii) failure [NS-1]. Profile facts were not used to decide the case [F16][F17].

rejected_claims.reason: A tap is only NS-1(i); the same record shows the tap at 12:06:15 was made 600 m from the pickup with 0 s inside the radius afterwards [F5], and the closest approach was 599 m [F1], so the tap does not make this a valid rider no-show under NS-1 [NS-1].

The 3 min 30 s stationary period occurred 600 m from the pickup [F2][F1], not at the pick-up location, so NS-1(iii) is not met; the written statement [F12] is contradicted by the GPS/timeline records, which prevail [NS-1].

Chat engagement does not put the car inside the arrival radius: the rider replied at 12:07 that she was at the pickup point with no car present [F9], while GPS never placed the driver within 200 m [F1][F5] [NS-1].

A complete, timestamped chat record [F11] does not supply the missing GPS elements: driver_arrived_at is null [F4] and the arrival tap was made 600 m out [F5], leaving NS-1(ii) and (iii) unsatisfied [NS-1].
Band 3 traffic on Jalan Besar with no incidents and fair weather [F13][F14][F15] does not excuse a stationary driver awaiting pickup 600 m from the pick-up point; NS-1 (ii)/(iii) still fail [NS-1].

The driver advocate's own fallback accepts the full return of the fee [F6]; the request to omit account action is not accepted because NS-2 attaches the flag where the arrival tap was made outside the pickup radius [F5][NS-2].
Profile facts [F17][F16] are not used to decide the case; the outcome rests on the GPS and timeline records [F1][F4][F5][NS-1].

The rider advocate's label of the flag as an NS-7 matter is misdirected: the account flag arises under NS-2 (fake arrival confirmation), while NS-7 only governs the voucher form of the refund [F5][F6][NS-2][NS-7].
